contract: construct() -> integer coefficients [c_0, ..., c_d] (constant term first) with 1 <= d <= 12, |c_i| <= 3 and c_d != 0. Polynomials equal to +-x^k times a product of cyclotomic polynomials (measure exactly one) are rejected by exact polynomial division. The score is the Mahler measure |c_d| * prod max(1, |z|) over all complex roots z (Aberth iteration, reported to 10 decimals). Minimize; the optimum is Lehmer's number 1.1762808183.
notes: Among integer polynomials of degree at most 12 the least measure above one is Lehmer's number, so the task recovers Lehmer's polynomial (up to sign, reversal and cyclotomic factors). Exact local certificates are not Lean proofs; the Mahler measure and reciprocal sums are reported as floats. Consult the independent oracle and malformed-input tests.

sources.locator: Michael J. Mossinghoff, Georges Rhin and Qiang Wu, Minimal Mahler Measures (2008). Crossref records inspected for Lehmer (Ann. of Math. 1933), Smyth (Bull. LMS 1971) and Mossinghoff, Rhin and Wu (Experimental Math. 2008). Lehmer's polynomial x^10 + x^9 - x^7 - x^6 - x^5 - x^4 - x^3 + x + 1 has measure 1.17628081826; Mossinghoff, Rhin and Wu determined the minimal measure of noncyclotomic irreducible polynomials of every even degree up to 54, none below Lehmer's number, and Smyth proved that nonreciprocal polynomials (which include every noncyclotomic irreducible polynomial of odd degree) have measure at least 1.3247. Measures multiply over factors, so no integer polynomial of degree at most 12 has measure in (1, 1.17628). Among integer polynomials of degree at most 12 the least measure above one is Lehmer's number, so the task recovers Lehmer's polynomial (up to sign, reversal and cyclotomic factors).
